tools.name: api_key_check
tools.description: Returns the user the key acts for, the user's plan and the key's scopes. Any live key can call it, so call it to test a key.

tools.name: contact_find
tools.description:

- `email` finds the contacts with that address. Case does not matter.
- `phone` finds the contacts with that number, however it is formatted.

tools.description:
Adds a contact. If the user already has this person, the values may go to that contact instead:

tools.name: contact_read
tools.description: Returns one contact. `id` is the contact's `id` or its `publicId`, such as `CS-0042`. A deleted or merged contact is a 404, and so is another user's contact.

tools.name: contact_change
tools.description:
Changes a contact, as editing it in ContactZapp does. Only the fields you send change. A field you leave out keeps its value.

The change goes to every two-way account the contact is in, never to a read-only one. History records it as the user's change and names the API key.

tools.name: sync_start
tools.description: Starts a sync, the same as Sync now in ContactZapp. History shows it as a manual run. The answer is 202 with the sync's state, `queued` or `running`. If a sync is already going, you get that one back and no second one starts.

tools.name: event_list
tools.description:
Lists the events of one type, newest first. Zapier, Make and n8n poll this to start an automation.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "event_list" stacks urgency/override words (never, attention). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: contact_find, contact_create, contact_change · Private data: api_key_check, contact_find, contact_create, contact_read, contact_change, event_list · Public sink: contact_find, contact_create, contact_change · Destructive: sync_start.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: contact_find, contact_create, contact_change · Private data: api_key_check, contact_find, contact_create, contact_read, contact_change, event_list · Public sink: contact_find, contact_create, contact_change · Destructive: sync_start

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
